-0.63634,51.60007.name: Lister Fertility Clinic at The Beaconsfield Clinic
-0.63634,51.60007.state: Little Hall Barn, Windsor End, Beaconsfield, Buckinghamshire, HP9 2JW
-0.63634,51.60007.company: Satellite clinic to The Lister Fertility Clinic
-0.63634,51.60007.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to The Lister Fertility Clinic. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-79.28731,43.72947.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, January 2025. -87.63600,41.87900.name: AUTM
-87.63600,41.87900.desc: The association of university technology transfer offices, which sets the norms for how publicly funded research is licensed to companies. The Bayh-Dole Act of 1980 let universities patent federally funded inventions, and this is the body that turned that into standard practice.

34.78180,32.08530.name: Tammuz Family
34.78180,32.08530.state: Tel Aviv — with offices across Europe, the Americas and Asia
34.78180,32.08530.desc: An Israeli agency founded in 2008, reporting more than 2,000 births and running programmes simultaneously in the United States, Georgia, Armenia, Mexico, Colombia, Argentina and Ukraine, with offices in more than a dozen further countries. Its group includes an egg donor agency and a chain of IVF clinics in Asia. The multi-jurisdiction structure is the entry, because it is the practical answer to everything else recorded in this facet: where a country closes, or announces it will, an agency operating in seven does not stop — it routes elsewhere and tells intended parents to compare the advantages and difficulties of each route. Note also the constraint it reports for one of those routes: Georgian law admits only heterosexual couples, married or cohabiting a year. The same agency therefore sells different eligibility rules depending on which country the pregnancy happens in.

-3.81000,40.34000.name: Vivotecnia
-3.81000,40.34000.desc: A Spanish contract research organisation operating since 2000, running toxicology and safety studies on monkeys, dogs, pigs, rabbits, rats and mice for the pharmaceutical, chemical, cosmetic, tobacco and food industries. In April 2021 an animal technician who had worked there between 2018 and 2020 released undercover footage through a campaign organisation; after an inspection the Madrid regional government said it had confirmed signs of mistreatment and suspended activity, and police animal protection services were contacted. The company's chief executive said he was shocked by the images. What happened next is the reason for the entry rather than the footage. The campaigners later reported that the suspension had covered only NEW projects while experiments already under way continued, that the animals were not rehomed as expected, and that testing was subsequently permitted to resume while legal action continued. The facility has held public research funding. A suspension that stops new work and leaves existing work running is a different instrument from the one the announcement describes, and this map should record which kind a regulator actually used.
